title: On the Memorization and Generalization of Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: The basis for the performance advantage of generative recommendation models over item ID-based models is unclear.

gap.claim: There is no systematic way to verify whether generative recommendation models generalize better beyond comparing overall performance.

contributions.claim: The authors categorize data instances by whether correct prediction requires memorization or generalization.
The authors analyze the divergence between generative recommendation and item ID-based models at the token level.
The authors propose a memorization-aware indicator that adaptively combines the two model paradigms on a per-instance basis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that generative recommendation models perform better on instances requiring generalization, while item ID-based models perform better when memorization is more important.
The authors report that apparent item-level generalization in generative recommendation models often reduces to token-level memorization.
The authors report improved overall recommendation performance from their memorization-aware indicator.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper examines the hypothesis that generative recommendation models outperform item ID-based models because they generalize better.
The authors identify the lack of a systematic verification method for this hypothesis.
They classify instances by the memorization or generalization capability required for correct prediction.
They report different strengths for the two model paradigms and attribute the generative models' apparent item-level generalization partly to token-level memorization.
They combine the complementary paradigms using a memorization-aware per-instance indicator.

source_observation.claim: Model performance differs depending on whether prediction requires memorization or generalization.

interpretation.claim: Evaluating models by capability-specific instance types can reveal complementary strengths hidden by aggregate performance.

application.claim: Use capability-aware instance categorization when comparing recommendation paradigms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how the instance categories are operationalized or how broadly the result transfers.

source_observation.claim: The two recommendation paradigms are reported to be complementary, and adaptive per-instance combination improves overall performance.

interpretation.claim: A hybrid system can exploit different model strengths according to instance requirements.

application.claim: Consider memorization-aware routing or combination for recommendation systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide details about the indicator, routing signals, or evaluation scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, or experiment settings.
The abstract does not describe the memorization-aware indicator's formulation or training procedure.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or limitations.
